# Primal attraction: channeling the Divine Masculine & Feminine
[NATIVE IMAGE — preserve from Substack source — https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/cbf41294-3c6b-4ac7-b5b6-dd52b242b919_1055x1491.png]
Everything I've been putting forward so far has leaned toward honesty, closeness, and equal dignity. I do believe in that basically for any type of relationship, but none of that by itself explains why two people still want to tear each other’s clothes off each night.
For me, safety gives the space for desire, even if it doesn't spark it.
When I feel safe with a woman, we can actually tell each other our fantasies without worrying that the other person is going to be horrified or weaponize it later. We can imagine pregnancy and really enjoy the thought that we might be making a baby, rather than imagining I’m ejaculating into a condom and hoping nothing happens.
Whenever I was scared of getting a woman pregnant, the sex was usually much more boring.
So why is it that a lot of relationship advice says desire needs distance, mystery, withholding, maybe even separate homes? I suspect they are compensating for a lack of expressed difference while together.
The more safety there is, the more closeness there is, the more polarity there needs to be to keep things alive and poppin'.
Some women may only get turned on by pathology and danger. A woman may also feel her man has become so feminine that there is no contrast left.
A lot of women want to feel that the man is dangerous in some way, but preferably in an exciting and defending way rather than threatening. Beauty and the Beast is a "tale as old as time" for a reason.
The real question is whether polarity stays alive inside the safety.
## Muses & Directors
In ordinary life, I sometimes think of the woman as the engine and myself as the steering wheel. I get motivation from her. She is the life force. She brings inspiration, beauty, intuition, creativity, and this feeling that life is worth doing.
I help give it direction and make it operational.
I find the intuitive mind incredibly sexy, because I can’t fully follow it. During sex, some of the most "womanly" women I’ve loved have gone through psychic experiences, memories that felt like past lives, and things I had no idea how to explain. One time, Bee said she almost got enlightened, but I came too fast. Woops...
Key could sometimes start talking and somehow teleport me outside the galaxy. I don’t know how else to describe it. Her voice would become so beautiful that I would shed tears that felt super liberating.
Bee could bring out something similar--she could be talking to me for hours on end, but instead of trying to mute her with the TV remote, I felt I was in a timeless dimension of love.
The muse gives the director his ineffable inspiration. She sees the big picture or feels something that has not become a plan yet. Then I have a chance to be useful by figuring out the details.
The muse can influence any decision where I ask for help, and also the decisions where she suddenly intuits that she has something important to add.
Micromanaging everything is totally different and not attractive. If she is refusing to trust my judgment, or simply taking over with “Let me do it,” I start feeling useless.
A woman can lead wherever the man is less sure. She may know more about any particular field, even a traditionally non-feminine one. The way she leads can still preserve the polarity of roles.
“Honey, let me help you with this,” is still sexy, but pushing him out of the way is not.
She can also receive his guidance without pretending he's always right. She might say, “Thank you, I’ll consider that. What do you think about doing it this way?” as a kind of gentle, almost hypnotic leadership. She is still influencing the direction he goes in without turning every disagreement into a contest over who is driving.
In my experience, women often prefer stronger and more direct leadership from a man:
“This is where I want to go. This is what I think we should do. Are you game?”
The woman may argue with the plan, change it, improve it, or refuse it. The masculine charge comes partly from directly offering a direction.
Equality in terms of dignity does not require both people to do every role equally.
Relationships work better when each person develops what they are good at, like specialization in any economy. That can be taken too far, of course. I’m not saying women should never learn to drive, nor that men should never cook. But if the man enjoys driving and the woman enjoys cooking, they can both usually do what makes them happiest.
Every respectful leader makes sure to take the other person’s ideas as serious input. Mandar obedeciendo, as the Zapatistas say.
The point is not to tally every act and force the totals to match.
## Desire is expressed differently for men & women
Women often show wanting directly. They ask, reach, name what they want, and ask the man to do things for them, even when they could do it themselves.
Men tend to show their wanting through providing, fixing, heavy labor, or trying to become indispensable. Not because men are less needy, but their neediness partly consists of being needed. Emotionally, women express their needs more, but this also allows them to get supported more often and by a wider social net. Men, on the other hand, tend to keep their needs to themselves or put them all onto their woman, especially when it comes to the need for a confidant.
If a man is too "needy," it tends to turn women off. The way women see it, a man should be in control of himself and able to satisfy his own basic needs. After all, how is he supposed to provide for somebody else if he can't manage himself?
It's not that male pursuit is a turn-off to women (assuming they are interested in the man), but they want to see that the man can pursue strongly while staying grounded. The polarity evaporates when he keeps reaching without satisfaction, loses control of himself, or makes the woman responsible for regulating his emotions.
## Not A Performance
I also don’t want masculinity or femininity to become an identity performance.
The moment I have to prove that I’m the man, something has already become fake. Then I have to defend the identity every time I hesitate, cry, need help, or get something wrong.
I don’t actually think of myself as especially masculine. I step into that energy when I see that a woman would appreciate it, and then it comes naturally. Bee once called me her “wife.” I don’t recommend that as a polarity exercise, by the way.
The same is true for a woman. She should not have to perform softness, helplessness, or cuteness every minute to prove she is feminine. Surrender means so much more when she could take control but prefers not to at that moment.
We can invite these energies out of each other gently.
“Honey, how do you see this intuitively?”
or, “Can you help me think through the practical side for a minute?”
That feels much better than, “Do your female/male thing now.”
When a strong woman surrenders, she is choosing to, which is sexy. She knows she could drive, but she asks you to drive, because she likes how it feels when you do.
That's called invitational: Would you rather go to a party where you were invited or a war you got drafted into?
When a woman doesn't know how to gently invite a man to lead, she may manufacture a crisis until the man is forced to take charge to get the same outward result.
Unfortunately, I've seen a lot of the latter.
## Fantasy
Inside real safety, people can turn the polarity dial all the way to the right.
Fantasy is one of the best ways to experiment with that. Domination fantasies are common in many forms, and they enable extreme masculine-feminine polarity without actual harm, because the real person still has consent and can stop.
Nobody is entitled to another person’s fantasies. They are private until the person decides to share them. When somebody does share one, it can be an extraordinary act of trust.
Esther Perel makes the distinction that fantasy is play rather than a real-life request. A rape fantasy is not a request to be raped in real life.
The couple can leave it in imagination or agree to bring some part of it into the room.
Fantasy should also add to arousal rather than become the only possible route to it. I want to be able to enjoy the actual woman and the actual experience too.
## The Queen of Orgasms
Many people are not even aware of how incredible sex can be when the polarity, trust, love & safety are all where they should be. Women have shown me that the cervix can open during sex and become intensely pleasurable for both of us. In fact, after you experience cervical sex, regular sex doesn't even seem like it's really "sex" anymore. It seems more like foreplay.
However, I've not yet very deeply "researched" these experiments, because "life" often got in the way, and building up to this actually takes a lot of "work" (ahem..).
Women describe cervical and whole-body orgasms very differently from the ordinary ones based on building friction toward release. Instead, cervical orgasms are more like being taken over by a profound energy running through the whole body.
Although the peanut gallery critics and lazy fact-checkers often cry fiction on this topic, Komisaruk and Whipple showed that cervical stimulation can produce orgasm even in women with a severed spinal cord, because the vagus nerve can carry the signal without using the spinal route that clitoral orgasms use. That laboratory evidence establishes the uniqueness of the phenomenon. Kim Anami, Diana Richardson, and other popular educators and promoters of cervical orgasms further claim that these can provide days of afterglow, as well as spiritual and physical healings.

# Twin Flames?
[NATIVE IMAGE — old source — https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/abc295d2-f1ec-414c-83e0-c4df99fe5de3_1024x1535.png]
In the previous section, I mentioned the divine feminine and divine masculine energies that you can channel to keep eroticism alive. But there’s really something more special about the in-love paradise that Twin Flames (TF) experience than a simple Divine Masculine + Divine Feminine formula. Maybe a better way to put it, as my friend Cody says, is Yin/Yang, which still has the masculine/feminine in it, but allows for a more broad type of complementary symbiosis.
There are a ton of people who don’t want to believe in twin flame theory because they haven’t found someone they could call their twin flame. That’s fine, and I am not trying to rock their boat. They might be the people who suggest that you should marry your best friend (or “soul mate” in the TF lingo). Then there are the folks who are deep in the TF theory, believing there is literally *one person* on Earth who is made for you. I’m also not trying to rock their boat. But I do want to tell my story.
I used to fall into the former camp, then into the latter camp, and now that I’ve experienced two twin flame relationships, I've jumped into a new camp I never knew existed.
## What two Twin Flames taught me
I used to think there was absolutely no way I could ever fall deeply in love with another woman after my 2nd wife, Bee. No other woman ever connected to me on such a deeply spiritual and deeply feminine level. I always said, Bee is the ultimate woman in every sense, but I also suspected I felt that way because of what I conceived a woman should be, and because of the shape of my own inner being. I could list her qualities which made me feel that way, but the sum total of the qualities would not produce what she represented. There was something deep and ineffable that I connected to with her. I truly understood the belief that your TF is really a half of your own soul (or of your own mind-stream in Buddhist terminology).
I wish I had a video to show you of me and Bee, but she was very camera-shy, and the only video that’s online of her is from when she graduated high school, but I still see the divinity in her in [that short clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HDVwi2jcpi4&t=99s) where she is the only one expressing that she wants to save others from going through what she’s gone through. I did make a video about how [I learned to love her instead of missing her](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/p/i-ate-loveyhuasca-every-day-for-90?r=5vdc6m) after we parted ways in 2020.
Then, in 2026, I met another Ultimate Woman, who even called herself “WOMAN” on her whatsapp profile, which I thought was hilarious and maybe a sign for me. You can see the video we made together while in love:
[NATIVE YOUTUBE — old source — videoId: ysZ_O50hhgM]
Falling in love with Key really blew my mind. How could it be possible to fall in love with a different woman? I thought Bee was my forever, only Twin. The conclusion seemed inexorable to me: Bee could not have been the only person on Earth with whom I could experience this. Key did not share that conclusion. But if both partners can accept it, I think de-ontologizing Twin Flames actually allows for a deeper sacred relationship.
## De-ontologizing Twin Flames FTW 💗
[NATIVE YOUTUBE — old source — videoId: Nc0NU5PWO8Q]
This part might seem unromantic to the TF community, but if people understood this, it would actually lead to much deeper unions and deeper love, in my opinion. I’ve basically synthesized the dialectic between the romance pragmatists who don’t believe in fairy tales and the fairy tale idealists who can’t understand why their relationships never work. If only I could find a woman who was on this same page with me. 😅
Basically, the Twin Flame experience is not about two unique people who must find each other against all odds. Well, they are uniquely matched in some ways, that’s true. But what’s really unique is that they are able to connect to each other’s deepest, most vulnerable corner of the heart.
When Key felt understood by me and safe with me during that first month, she would naturally slip into her divine-feminine sacred-partner archetype. Bee did the same every other day. In that state I was the ultimate treasure in the universe to them, and they seemed able to reside safely in every part of their minds and hearts. The safety brought out their infinite cuteness, beauty, innocence, gratitude, inspiration, creativity, and even a particular ***voice*** that emblematized all of it. It made me like a love-slave with no sense of free will!
Anyway. If we don’t understand that the Twin Flame is an energy that a person can access… if we conflate the person’s egoic flaws that actually annoy us with their deepest, truest, most beautiful self, then we end up playing John Legend on loop like my first wife, Ann, who held me up to this standard, wondering why I didn’t praise her for her imperfections:
[NATIVE YOUTUBE — old source — videoId: 450p7goxZqg]
Ok I’m not trying to bash John Legend nor *All of Me*. It’s one of the most beautiful, most hopeless romantic songs in history. And there’s a part of it which really does apply to what I’m talking about because for your partner to feel truly safe with you, they have to know you accept all of them. But there’s a toxic part there which is that if you *just* accept everything, you’re a yes man, a doormat, nothing actually special, and you’re inviting them to shit-test you.
If you really loved them, more than just wanting to enjoy them or keep them, you’d want to *be a good influence* on them. That means showing them the infinite appreciation you have for their divine, inner-child-higher self, and holding their hand to gently guide them back to that deeply authentic part of themself when they get off track—if that is where they want to go. Making it clear that that’s why you’re in love with them. Not because they are imperfect, not because you’re crazy and desperate. You accept the imperfect person and help them move toward the part of themselves they chose, because you want to “Make them move with confidence” like the [Faker song “Talk is cheap.”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z8Wjdss5uMg)

# Two Pillars Don't Hold The Roof Up
Even if you find your twin flame, she’s still only one person, and that's more of a problem than it seems at first. Polarity does not make two people sufficient for each other. A couple still needs friends and community.
Let me show you how this looked for me. I’ve noticed in my own relationships that whenever a serious issue arises, both of us tend to turn to our separate circles of friends for support. Then I resent the one-sided story she’s telling, she resents the one-sided story I’m telling, and eventually neither of us wants to talk to the other’s friends. Some of the friends may even be exes who want us to break up. By then, the outside support isn’t really shared support anymore.
When you rely on your partner to provide nearly all the friendship, family, therapy, and spiritual meaning, the burden is overwhelming. That's too many hats to wear even for a hat model. Besides all that, there's no security when two people have to cover all the life essentials: housing, money, children, emotional, health, and other crises. Who even has time for the relationship itself at that point?
Romantic love can last, but it needs the right conditions, and community is one of them. Both people have to support it, and support from a community makes that much more realistic.
Community isn’t magic either. A very strong couple without much trauma can often do well without community, although it’s a struggle and I think it’s rare. A weak couple might not work even with a community if both people are too weak individually. It depends on the couple.
But having more people around the relationship changes what the two people have to carry. Mutual friends can notice patterns neither person sees. Somebody else can comfort your partner when you have become the wrong person to do it. And when people actually know both of you, they have some chance of telling when the story they’re hearing does not match the person they know.
That's not abstract to me: I'm sure B. and I would still be together if we'd had a real community around us. Most of all, she would not have been capable of demonizing me when everyone already knew both of us and knew I wasn’t a narcissistic abuser. It would have contained all the insanity. Baseless accusations only work with friends who only know one side.
Commune friends could also have helped her in ways I couldn’t, because she was projecting onto me, which made me the wrong person to help her see beyond the projection. And it's actually natural to be a bit BPD when your entire survival depends on one person, because if they aren't perfect, and especially if you need a lot of support, how will you survive? One fairly normal but large flaw in them could make your life really difficult. We were left alone inside something that needed other people around it, and that's what's happening to most people these days.
H. taught me another part of the same dyad problem. I learned not to treat what either of us thought the relationship was as a guarantee of what it would remain, because feelings can and usually do change over time. In our case, the relationship continued to naturally deepen while our outside relationships often felt more shallow, so it was natural for the dependency to increase. She was never into monogamy, but that didn't stop her from becoming possessive once she found something really worth keeping. And then she began demonizing me when I refused to be possessed. Because we did not have a shared community capable of supporting us, her friends heard her side and affirmed her truth. The accusations couldn't have survived among people who knew us both.
Separate confidants can be helpful and harmful. Sometimes you need privacy from your partner and somewhere else to say what you’re feeling. But if your confidant doesn’t have a good connection with your partner, the conversation can turn into an echo chamber very easily.
Having the same confidant creates the opposite problem: now you may not have a release valve when you want privacy from your partner. There isn’t one perfect arrangement.
If you do have separate confidants, you need enough emotional maturity to remember they will automatically be biased toward you. Take what they say with a grain of salt. They are hearing a partial story, usually while you’re upset, and they may be trying to protect you rather than understand the relationship fairly.
So if you don't have a real community already, what can you do about it practically, right now?
Make as much community as you can wherever you are. Go to meetups together. Make deep friendships together. Find some shared purpose beyond maintaining the relationship. Introduce your old friends to your partner and try to mutualize those friendships as much as possible, so they aren’t experienced as slyly antagonistic or partial to one side. You don’t need to spend all your time together, but two completely separate social worlds will automatically start taking sides when something goes wrong.
I do think romantic love can last for a lifetime. I just don't think two people should have to become each other's entire social world to keep it alive. So keep your friendships. They aren't automatically a threat to the relationship; they're part of what keeps you healthy enough to be in one.

# Two Pillars Don't Hold The Roof Up
Even if you find your twin flame, she’s still only one person, and that's more of a problem than it seems at first. Polarity does not make two people sufficient for each other. A couple still needs friends and community.
Let me show you how this looked for me. I’ve noticed in my own relationships that whenever a serious issue arises, both of us tend to turn to our separate circles of friends for support. Then I resent the one-sided story she’s telling, she resents the one-sided story I’m telling, and eventually neither of us wants to talk to the other’s friends. Some of the friends may even be exes who want us to break up. By then, the outside support isn’t really shared support anymore.
When you rely on your partner to provide nearly all the friendship, family, therapy, and spiritual meaning, the burden is overwhelming. That's too many hats to wear even for a hat model. Besides all that, there's no security when two people have to cover all the life essentials: housing, money, children, emotional, health, and other crises. Who even has time for the relationship itself at that point?
Romantic love can last, but it needs the right conditions, and community is one of them. Both people have to support it, and support from a community makes that much more realistic.
Community isn’t magic either. A very strong couple without much trauma can often do well without community, although it’s a struggle and I think it’s rare. A weak couple might not work even with a community if both people are too weak individually. It depends on the couple.
But having more people around the relationship changes what the two people have to carry. Mutual friends can notice patterns neither person sees. Somebody else can comfort your partner when you have become the wrong person to do it. And when people actually know both of you, they have some chance of telling when the story they’re hearing does not match the person they know.
That's not abstract to me: I'm sure B. and I would still be together if we'd had a real community around us. Most of all, she would not have been capable of demonizing me when everyone already knew both of us and knew I wasn’t a narcissistic abuser. It would have contained all the insanity. Baseless accusations only work with friends who only know one side.
Commune friends could also have helped her in ways I couldn’t, because she was projecting onto me, which made me the wrong person to help her see beyond the projection. And it's actually natural to be a bit BPD when your entire survival depends on one person, because if they aren't perfect, and especially if you need a lot of support, how will you survive? One fairly normal but large flaw in them could make your life really difficult. We were left alone inside something that needed other people around it, and that's what's happening to most people these days.
H. taught me another part of the same dyad problem. I learned not to treat what either of us thought the relationship was as a guarantee of what it would remain, because feelings can and usually do change over time. In our case, the relationship continued to naturally deepen while our outside relationships often felt more shallow, so it was natural for the dependency to increase. She was never into monogamy, but that didn't stop her from becoming possessive once she found something really worth keeping. And then she began demonizing me when I refused to be possessed. Because we did not have a shared community capable of supporting us, her friends heard her side and affirmed her truth. The accusations couldn't have survived among people who knew us both.
Separate confidants can be helpful and harmful. Sometimes you need privacy from your partner and somewhere else to say what you’re feeling. But if your confidant doesn’t have a good connection with your partner, the conversation can turn into an echo chamber very easily.
Having the same confidant creates the opposite problem: now you may not have a release valve when you want privacy from your partner. There isn’t one perfect arrangement.
If you do have separate confidants, you need enough emotional maturity to remember they will automatically be biased toward you. Take what they say with a grain of salt. They are hearing a partial story, usually while you’re upset, and they may be trying to protect you rather than understand the relationship fairly.
So if you don't have a real community already, what can you do about it practically, right now?
Make as much community as you can wherever you are. Go to meetups together. Make deep friendships together. Find some shared purpose beyond maintaining the relationship. Introduce your old friends to your partner and try to mutualize those friendships as much as possible, so they aren’t experienced as slyly antagonistic or partial to one side. You don’t need to spend all your time together, but two completely separate social worlds will automatically start taking sides when something goes wrong.
I do think romantic love can last for a lifetime. I just don't think two people should have to become each other's entire social world to keep it alive. So keep your friendships. They aren't automatically a threat to the relationship; they're part of what keeps you healthy enough to be in one.

The real question is whether polarity stays alive inside the safety.

## Muses & Directors

In ordinary life, I sometimes think of the woman as the engine and myself as the steering wheel. I get motivation from her. She is the life force. She brings inspiration, beauty, intuition, creativity, and this feeling that life is worth doing.

I help give it direction and make it operational.

One time, Bee said she almost got enlightened, but I came too fast. Woops...

Key could sometimes start talking and somehow teleport me outside the galaxy. I don’t know how else to describe it. Her voice would become so beautiful that I would shed tears that felt super liberating.

Bee could bring out something similar--she could be talking to me for hours on end, but instead of trying to mute her with the TV remote, I felt I was in a timeless dimension of love.

The muse gives the director his ineffable inspiration. She sees the big picture or feels something that has not become a plan yet. Then I have a chance to be useful by figuring out the details.

The muse can influence any decision where I ask for help, and also the decisions where she suddenly intuits that she has something important to add.

Micromanaging everything is totally different and not attractive. If she is refusing to trust my judgment, or simply taking over with “Let me do it,” I start feeling useless.

A woman can lead wherever the man is less sure. She may know more about any particular field, even a traditionally non-feminine one. The way she leads can still preserve the polarity of roles.

“Honey, let me help you with this,” is still sexy, but pushing him out of the way is not.

She can also receive his guidance without pretending he's always right. She might say, “Thank you, I’ll consider that. What do you think about doing it this way?” as a kind of gentle, almost hypnotic leadership. In my experience, women often prefer stronger and more direct leadership from a man:

“This is where I want to go. This is what I think we should do. Are you game?”

The woman may argue with the plan, change it, improve it, or refuse it. The masculine charge comes partly from directly offering a direction.

Equality in terms of dignity does not require both people to do every role equally.

Relationships work better when each person develops what they are good at, like specialization in any economy. That can be taken too far, of course. I’m not saying women should never learn to drive, nor that men should never cook. But if the man enjoys driving and the woman enjoys cooking, they can both usually do what makes them happiest.

Every respectful leader makes sure to take the other person’s ideas as serious input. Mandar obedeciendo, as the Zapatistas say.

The point is not to tally every act and force the totals to match.

## Desire is expressed differently for men & women

Women often show wanting directly. They ask, reach, name what they want, and ask the man to do things for them, even when they could do it themselves.

Men tend to show their wanting through providing, fixing, heavy labor, or trying to become indispensable. Not because men are less needy, but their neediness partly consists of being needed. Emotionally, women express their needs more, but this also allows them to get supported more often and by a wider social net. Men, on the other hand, tend to keep their needs to themselves or put them all onto their woman, especially when it comes to the need for a confidant.

If a man is too "needy," it tends to turn women off. The way women see it, a man should be in control of himself and able to satisfy his own basic needs. After all, how is he supposed to provide for somebody else if he can't manage himself?

It's not that male pursuit is a turn-off to women (assuming they are interested in the man), but they want to see that the man can pursue strongly while staying grounded. The polarity evaporates when he keeps reaching without satisfaction, loses control of himself, or makes the woman responsible for regulating his emotions.

I also don’t want masculinity or femininity to become an identity performance.

The moment I have to prove that I’m the man, something has already become fake. Then I have to defend the identity every time I hesitate, cry, need help, or get something wrong.

I don’t actually think of myself as especially masculine. I step into that energy when I see that a woman would appreciate it, and then it comes naturally. Bee once called me her “wife.” I don’t recommend that as a polarity exercise, by the way.

The same is true for a woman. She should not have to perform softness, helplessness, or cuteness every minute to prove she is feminine. Surrender means so much more when she could take control but prefers not to at that moment.

We can invite these energies out of each other gently.

“Honey, how do you see this intuitively?”

or, “Can you help me think through the practical side for a minute?”

That feels much better than, “Do your female/male thing now.”

When a strong woman surrenders, she is choosing to, which is sexy. She knows she could drive, but she asks you to drive, because she likes how it feels when you do.

That's called invitational: Would you rather go to a party where you were invited or a war you got drafted into?

When a woman doesn't know how to gently invite a man to lead, she may manufacture a crisis until the man is forced to take charge to get the same outward result.

Unfortunately, I've seen a lot of the latter.

Inside real safety, people can turn the polarity dial all the way to the right.

Fantasy is one of the best ways to experiment with that. Domination fantasies are common in many forms, and they enable extreme masculine-feminine polarity without actual harm, because the real person still has consent and can stop.

Nobody is entitled to another person’s fantasies. They are private until the person decides to share them. When somebody does share one, it can be an extraordinary act of trust.

Esther Perel makes the distinction that fantasy is play rather than a real-life request. A rape fantasy is not a request to be raped in real life.

The couple can leave it in imagination or agree to bring some part of it into the room.

Fantasy should also add to arousal rather than become the only possible route to it. I want to be able to enjoy the actual woman and the actual experience too.

Many people are not even aware of how incredible sex can be when the polarity, trust, love & safety are all where they should be. Women have shown me that the cervix can open during sex and become intensely pleasurable for both of us. In fact, after you experience cervical sex, regular sex doesn't even seem like it's really "sex" anymore. It seems more like foreplay.

However, I've not yet very deeply "researched" these experiments, because "life" often got in the way, and building up to this actually takes a lot of "work" (ahem..).

Women describe cervical and whole-body orgasms very differently from the ordinary ones based on building friction toward release. Instead, cervical orgasms are more like being taken over by a profound energy running through the whole body.

Although the peanut gallery critics and lazy fact-checkers often cry fiction on this topic, Komisaruk and Whipple showed that cervical stimulation can produce orgasm even in women with a severed spinal cord, because the vagus nerve can carry the signal without using the spinal route that clitoral orgasms use.
